RetailMax Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the RetailMax Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, participants are required to use their handsets to ask questions. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss RetailMax Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report RetailMax Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Let me start by sharing highlights from our overall company performance this quarter, which ended on September 28th. We posted net sales of $2.48 billion, reflecting a 4.2% increase year-over-year and marking our third straight quarter of positive top-line momentum. This beat the midpoint of our guidance and highlights the durability of our brick-and-mortar foundation, which still powers 82% of total sales through our omnichannel approach.

Core same-store sales, covering stores open at least 14 months and incorporating BOPIS and ship-from-store activity, climbed 3.1% worldwide, with U.S. comps at 3.4%. That came from 1.5% higher store traffic paired with 1.6% more transactions per customer visit. Average unit retail stayed firm at $52.30, edging up 0.2%, as we prioritized value assortments like our growing private-label Summit Home Essentials collection, which delivered 15% comp gains in kitchenware and bedding. Conversion rose 2.1%, aided by in-store digital kiosks from our Zebra Technologies RFID collaboration, cutting out-of-stocks 22% and giving associates instant inventory access.

Gross profit hit $955 million, or 38.5% of sales, expanding 120 basis points year-over-year. Merchandise margins improved 180 basis points from fewer markdowns and a shift to stronger apparel and home categories, though offset somewhat by 60 basis points of freight pressure from Red Sea issues. Shrink eased 10 basis points to 1.6% of sales, beating our 1.7% goal, thanks to the Eagle Eye AI loss prevention rollout across 85% of our 1,250 stores using computer vision.

Adjusted EBITDA was $352 million, or 14.2% of sales, up 18% year-over-year with 110 basis points of expansion. SG&A came down 90 basis points to 23.9% of sales, driven by smarter labor via Kronos scheduling and 5% lower corporate costs under our Fit-for-Growth program. Diluted EPS reached $0.87, topping consensus by $0.09.

By region, the Sunbelt shone brightest, with Southeast and Southwest comps up 5.8% in Florida, Texas, and Arizona stores, boosted by population shifts and tourism recovery, much like Home Depot's big-ticket home strength. Midwest comps were flat at 0.1%, hit by odd weather but lifted by back-to-school in juniors apparel rivaling Dillard's. Northeast comps grew 1.2%, pressured by inflation and reduced urban office traffic, but our refreshed experiential stores in Manhattan and Boston—with interactive shop-with-me areas and AR mirrors—quadrupled dwell times and added 12% to comps there.

We're leveraging the brick-and-mortar resurgence strategically. Digital sales via app, site, and marketplaces rose 12% to $446 million, or 18% of total, with store-fulfilled orders up 25% through curbside and BOPIS, making our stores the cost-effective fulfillment backbone against Amazon. Portfolio-wise, we opened 12 compact urban formats under 20,000 square feet in Atlanta and Phoenix while shuttering 18 low performers in secondary Midwest spots, trimming square footage 2% but boosting sales per foot to $620 for 150 basis points more EBITDA.

Traction is building on fronts like Summit Loyalty+, now with 28 million actives up 22%, driving 45% of sales at double the non-member AUR, echoing Ulta's model. Supply chain de-risking includes dual-sourcing 40% of imports from Vietnam and Mexico, shortening leads 15 days ahead of tariffs. Sustainability via recycled apparel with Recover Brands added $120 million in sales and 300 basis points to margins, appealing to Gen Z.

Forward, consumers are split—strong on home consumables, cautious on fashion amid job worries. We stand by full-year comps of 2.5-3.5%, 75-100 basis points gross margin growth, and 50+ basis points EBITDA expansion, backed by $250 million capex for 75 remodels and micro-fulfillment.

Shifting to e-commerce growth, which stood out as a top-line engine in this tough brick-and-mortar climate. E-commerce sales hit $285 million, up a strong 28% from $222 million last Q3 FY2023, our 11th straight double-digit quarter, beating the U.S. retail e-comm average of 12% per Census data. Digital now makes up 22% of net sales, from 17% a year ago and 14% two years back, holding us competitively versus Williams-Sonoma's 65% while our 1,200+ stores differentiate our hybrid model.

Key drivers included 32% YoY traffic jump to 45 million uniques, powered by $15 million more in digital marketing, dropping CAC to $28 per new customer—down 15%—via optimized Google Ads and TikTok Shop for Gen Z on Essentials Edge cookware. Conversions hit 4.2% from 3.6%, thanks to Dynamic Yield AI personalization lifting add-to-cart 18% in bedding and outdoor furniture. AOV rose 14% to $185 with bundles like smart home kits and subscriptions for filters and cleaners, now 8% of recurring e-comm revenue.

Our headless Shopify Plus shift integrates store inventory for BOPIS at 42% of orders, up from 35%, with 450 stores as micro-hubs cutting delivery under two hours in 75% urban areas via DoorDash. Fulfillment stayed at 12% of sales. U.S. led at 31% growth to $210 million, strong Northeast/West Coast; Sunbelt rural up 22% with new Phoenix/Atlanta DCs. International $75 million up 18%, Europe 25% on UK/Germany sites, Canada 12% softer but promo-boosted.

This reinforces our Stores as Hubs strategy—e-comm margins at 42%, 200 bps over stores, lifting store traffic 5% and 28% online-to-offline conversions. Q4 eyes 25-30% growth, $120 million Black Friday Cyber Week GMV up 35%, AR room planners next month. No store cannibalization, comps +4.2%. E-comm fortifies our moat in the $800 billion home goods space.

Turning to store performance, our key strategic initiatives under the Forge Forward banner—launched last year across our 1,200 stores—are advancing sharply. With industry comps at +1.2% per NRF amid inflation, apparel/home softness, and Amazon's 38% online share, our four pillars—store optimization, omnichannel, supply chain resilience, customer innovation—are delivering.

On store optimization, we closed 75 underperformers—mostly small Midwest Ohio/Michigan formats amid 4.8% unemployment—and opened 25 Sunbelt flagships in Texas/Florida, 50,000 sq ft with Target-like experiential zones. 180 YTD remodels added open-sell, BOPIS hubs, RFID shelves, slashing out-of-stocks 22%, turning inventory 4.2x to 5.1x. Remodeled comps +14.7% vs chain +5.2%, traffic +9% per Placer.ai, margins +120 bps to 42.1% via AI planograms. H2 targets 100 more in Atlanta/Phoenix high-income areas.

Omnichannel hit 28% sales, up from 19%, topping McKinsey's 5%; BOPIS 32% digital orders vs Home Depot's 17%, cutting costs 35%. Curbside at 85% stores, digital comps +41%. Snapchat AR app like Macy's got 150K downloads, apparel conversions +18%. Ship-from-store 22% e-comm. Northeast +22% digital despite tourism dip.

Supply chain resilience countered 15% freight hikes with $250M domestic/micro-fulfillment; new Georgia/Nevada DCs total 12M sq ft, Asia leads -28% to 21 days. Vendor direct 45% SKUs like Costco, fill rates 98.2%. AI vision at 400 stores cut ORC losses 11% to 1.2%, +90 bps margins.

Customer innovation: MaxRewards 18.2M members up 28%, Adobe personalization +24% ticket to $128. Max Moments geo-flashes +16% unplanned buys. Private label 35%, recycled packaging -52% plastic, Gen Z 22% traffic. West Coast 35% loyalty with EV chargers.

Compounding: optimized EBITDA 12.4% vs 8.1%, $450M FY synergies, $120M SG&A. 65/35 store/digital hedges returns (8% vs Amazon 15%). Midwest risk caps H2 comps 4-6%, Sunbelt tailwind. $300M CapEx, 60% tech stores, mid-teens ROIC. Q2 EPS beat 15%, FY $2.85-3.05 raised.

Marketing initiatives also progressed thoughtfully. Expenses totaled $128 million, +12% YoY or 4.2% of sales vs 3.8% prior and 4.5% Q1, showing efficiencies from programmatic/retail media as we geared for back-to-school/holidays in a tough environment with inflation, discretionary weakness, Amazon/Wayfair pressure.

Digital 62% of spend at $79M +18% YoY: Google/Meta/TikTok, our HERMN beta like Walmart Connect/Target Roundel at 4.5x ROAS, $45M sales. First-party clean rooms cut CAC 22% to $18.50 vs industry $25. Google CPM $2.45 steady, Trade Desk AI bids; TikTok UGC 3.2x ROAS for DIY youth.

Traditional/in-store 28% $36M +5%: Hulu/Roku CTV 2.8x ROAS for 35-54 demo; AR mirrors in 450 stores +15% conversion/$145 AOV; local OOH geo-fenced to app. Partnerships 10% $13M with Whirlpool/Sherwin-Williams offsetting 40%, $220M incremental.

Sunbelt +15% for openings (Phoenix/Atlanta housing +8%), CAC $16; Northeast +8% retention SMS/email 42% open/4.1% CTR; Canada flat CAD12M, Quebec 3.5x.

Efficiency playbook: 150 bps reallocated via GA4/MMM from print (<5%) to TV/social. HERMN monetization $50M FY25 target, 5% sales. Q3 4.0-4.3%, $20M holiday, GenAI +25% ROAS. FY 3.9-4.1%, $1.2B revenue, CLV $850.

On supply chain optimization, we've built buffers: new DCs slashed leads, vendor programs boosted fills, AI curbed shrink—key to resilience.

We're confident in navigating headwinds and creating shareholder value long-term.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to detail financials.

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $15.4 billion, a 5.1% increase compared to the same period last year.

Gross margin was 28.2%, down 110 basis points YoY, primarily driven by inventory shrinkage pressures, though offset by mix improvements.

Before moving on, let me expand on that key headwind: inventory shrinkage—or shrink—across our brick-and-mortar operations with over 1,800 high-traffic stores akin to Home Depot and Lowe's peers. Shrink includes external theft like shoplifting and organized retail crime, internal associate/vendor theft, admin errors in cycle counts, and damage/spoilage. It raises COGS, squeezing margins without revenue gain.

Q3 shrink was 1.85% of net sales, +15 bps YoY, a $285 million drag on our $15.4 billion top line, equating to 95 bps impact on the 28.2% margin. Absent this, adjusted margin would've gained 15 bps sequentially, aligning with 2-3% comps in power tools, lumber, softlines.

By category: external theft 52% or 96 bps, from ORC on high-value items like Milwaukee drills, DeWalt tools, electronics—8% sales, 35% shrink dollars. Internal 22% vendor fraud in paint/seasonal; admin/damage 26%. Matches NRF 1.6% 2023 average, but our ORC categories 20-30% higher.

Trends: up from 1.4% FY2021 to 1.7% FY2022, 1.75% through Q2, Q3 tick-up from back-to-school/holiday. Flat seq from Q2 1.84%, but YoY from post-COVID deterrence drop, Prop 47 limits, +25% ORC per our data. Peers: Target 1.9%/100 bps hit; Walmart 1.2% via scale.

Regional: Pacific urban (CA/OR/WA, 22% sales/38% shrink) 2.4%, smash-grabs on appliances/power gear; LA +40% tool thefts like Home Depot. Midwest/SE suburban 1.3-1.5% with policing. Canada 150 stores 1.6% enforcement edge.

Response under Fortress Retail: $450M FY2024 +18% YoY for tech/process/ecosystem. Verkada/Standard Cognition AI vision 65% stores (100% YE), -22% detection time, recovery 12% to 28%. RFID 45% high-shrink SKUs (tools/grills/cosmetics) -15 bps admin, full Q1. SCO 35% txns with nudges/rovers -30% shrink pilots. Weekly cycles top-shrink stores via Manhattan WMS, ShrinkScore ML dashboard.

Partnerships: RILA ORC task force, 150+ arrests YTD incl Bay Area $2.5M tool ring. Shrink-neutral pricing 12% assortment, supplier talks absorb 20 bps vs pass-through, holds EDLP vs Amazon/Costco.

Q4 expect 1.75-1.80% moderation: greeters/keepers/GenAI LP. FY 1.8% -10 bps YoY, 40-50 bps FY2025 tailwind vs NRF 1.7%, to 28.5-29% medium. $1.1B industry friction to moat.

Operating expenses were $4.1 billion, representing 26.6% of revenue.

Net income was $450 million, or $0.65 per share.

We generated $800 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory levels are currently optimized, down 3% year-over-year with improved turns.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Taylor Kim, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines.

Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we launched our Forge Essentials line of power tools and home improvement gear, which has seen exceptional sell-through rates 25% ahead of plan and strong initial customer feedback across our high-traffic categories. Early indicators show robust velocity in both stores and online, with particular strength in cordless drills and seasonal outdoor items. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in apparel-adjacent softlines next quarter.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, participants are required to use their handsets to ask questions. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of shrink and theft on your margins?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Mike. As Jordan detailed, shrink was a notable pressure at 1.85%, up slightly YoY, but our multi-faceted Fortress Retail efforts—including AI vision rollout to 65% of stores, RFID expansion, and ORC partnerships yielding over 150 arrests—are already showing results like improved recovery rates and targeted interventions in high-risk urban areas. We're on track for moderation ahead and see this as a path to margin outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, Lisa. We're guiding to 3-5% comp growth in Q4, building on this quarter's 3.1% with tailwinds from holiday ramps, Sunbelt strength, and omnichannel lifts like BOPIS at 32% of digital. Risks like Midwest softness are offset by loyalty-driven traffic and remodel momentum delivering +14% in upgraded units.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Wong (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, David. Our resilience pillar has been pivotal—with new DCs in Georgia and Nevada expanding to 12 million sq ft, lead times from Asia down 28% to 21 days, vendor direct covering 45% SKUs at 98.2% fill rates, and AI curbing ORC for 90 bps margin help. Dual-sourcing to Vietnam/Mexico de-risks tariffs, positioning us strongly for holiday volume.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's question-and-answer session.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
